The nucleus is a packed cluster of proton and neutron spheres around a white-hot core that lights everything near it; three tilted neon orbit rings carry racing electrons that leave rainbow trails. Real volumetric light: sun shafts through haze, soft shadows, and god rays cast outward from the core through the spinning rings. Electron and core light pools onto the floor, the floor mirrors the atom, fog eats the distance. HDR bloom, exposure, ACES tone mapping, film grain. Palette morphs Prism → Classic → Candy, hues cycle; Background Color tints the void (a light colour turns the frame into airbrushed paper). Bass swells the core and the shafts, mids push the electrons and ring glow, highs twinkle the sparkles, beats flash the sun.

Bokeh sparkles drift in depth with a shallow depth of field, soft bloom, film grain. Background colour is yours to set — pale studio grey, white paper or black glass. Bass breathes and spins the helix, mids light the rungs, highs twinkle the bokeh, beats flash the key light.

description: Bismuth — an alien hopper-crystal megastructure floating in deep space. A vast square funnel of stair-stepped terraces (the way real bismuth grows, edges outrunning faces) in dark iridescent metal: every terrace carries a different oxide thickness so the steps shift violet, teal, gold and magenta as the camera orbits. A plasma core burns at the bottom of the pit and lights the funnel walls from below; circuit seams glow along every terrace edge with pulses running round them; a scanner plane sweeps up the structure; newly grown terraces come in white-hot and cool to colour; smaller shard crystals drift around the mother structure. Volumetric fog fills the pit and a column of light climbs out of it; stars and nebula behind. Bass drives the core and the seams, mids shift the oxide colours, highs sparkle the edges, beats fire a pulse ring out through the terraces.
title: Bismuth

description: Molecules — ball-and-stick chemistry in a lit 3D studio. Real molecules tumble in from the fog, meet over a glossy floor and REACT: bonds shiver harder and harder, dissolve in a flash, and the atoms re-pair into the products (CO2, water, ammonia, ethane…) which drift apart and leave, then the next reaction rolls in — hydrogen burning (2 H2 + O2 → 2 H2O), methane combustion, the Haber process, ethene hydrogenation, carbon monoxide oxidation and benzene's Kekulé resonance flip. Atoms are glossy CPK-coloured spheres (carbon dark, hydrogen white, oxygen red, nitrogen blue) with Fresnel rims, crisp speculars, soft key-light shadows and contact occlusion; bonds are two-tone rods, double and triple bonds as twin and triple rods; an optional electron cloud glows around the atoms. Bass shakes the bonds, beats flash the rods white, highs sparkle the highlights, the level lifts the key light.
title: Molecules

description: Reaction — a living Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion chemistry rendered as 3D relief: two chemicals feed and kill each other in a real simulation (six solver steps every frame), and the growing concentration is raised into a landscape of coral ridges, dividing cells, wandering worms, fingerprint ridges, pulsing solitons or drifting spots that keep spreading, splitting and healing while a low camera drifts and orbits over them. Ridges glow hot, valleys hold a deep subsurface tint, a key light throws soft shadows across the relief with crisp speculars, rim light and a haze toward the horizon. Fresh seeds keep landing so the chemistry never dies. Bass pulses the growth and lifts the relief, beats splash new seeds, mids stir the field, highs sparkle the ridges.
title: Reaction

description: Bubbles — effervescence seen from inside the liquid: gas nucleates on the floor of a vessel and along a submerged electrode wire, and streams of bubbles rise through a deep tinted liquid toward a rippling silver surface. Every bubble is a real raymarched gas pocket — it swells as the pressure drops, wobbles into an oblate wobbling shape, zig-zags sideways, and the fast big ones catch and swallow the slow small ones in a soft coalescence that flashes iridescent. Thin-film interference paints rainbow bands across each bubble that drift as the film drains with age; the liquid behind is bent through the gas, the rims flare with total internal reflection and a hot key-light glint, and a lens caustic focuses under each bubble onto the caustic-lit floor. Light shafts fall from the surface, the surface mirrors the rising bubbles and rings outward where each one pops, micro-bubble sparkle streams twinkle between the columns. Bass swells the bubbles, beats release a burst of fizz and flash the key light, highs twinkle the sparkles, level lifts the shafts.
title: Bubbles

description: Orbitals — the electron clouds of a hydrogen atom rendered as real quantum probability: 1s, 2s, 2p, 3d, 4f and sp³ hybrid wavefunctions (exact Laguerre radial × spherical harmonic forms) raymarched as glowing volumetric density, the two phase signs of the wavefunction painted in two colours. The atom cycles through orbitals with quantum jumps: the cloud collapses toward the nucleus, a photon flash bursts out as an expanding ring of light, and the next orbital blooms open. Nested probability shells flow outward through the cloud as thin crisp iso-lines, the nucleus burns white at the centre, electron dust specks orbit through the field, and a faint lab-floor grid grounds it all. Or dial any orbital by hand and morph between neighbours. Bass swells the cloud, mids spin the phase, highs twinkle the dust, beats fire a photon flash.
title: Orbitals

description: Plotter — a pen plotter drawing 3D scenes as line art, live. Raymarched scenes (stacked blocks, the classic sphere-and-cube CSG with drilled holes, a rippling function plot, a striped skyscraper city, a torus and a sphere lattice) are rendered the way a vector plotter would see them: silhouette and crease edges, contour and grid lines laid on every surface, three levels of hatching where the light falls off, hidden lines removed. The pen plots each sheet stroke by stroke with a glowing pen head and wet-ink highlight, holds the finished drawing, lifts the page and starts the next scene from a new angle — a continuous plotting session. Hand-shake squiggle, pen pressure, ink bleed, paper grain, two pens (edges and hatching) on dark or cream paper. Bass thickens the pen, mids push the plot along, highs shake the hand, the level brightens the ink.
title: Plotter

description: Veins — a living network of chrome roots and veins in 3D. Three families of wavy vessels thread through a slowly writhing space and meet at real junctions, so the tangle branches like roots: thick trunks, medium veins and fine capillaries, all in mirror chrome reflecting a dark studio with magenta, cyan and amber lights. Pulses travel along every vessel as peristaltic bulges, glowing faintly from inside as they pass, and the camera glides endlessly forward through a clear channel in the tangle while the whole network breathes and drifts. Chrome inter-reflections, Fresnel, three-colour glints, ambient occlusion, depth fog, bloom and film grain. Bass swells the pulses, mids speed the flow, highs twinkle the glints, beats fire a bright pulse down the vessels.
title: Veins

description: Physarum — a real slime mould. Hundreds of thousands of agents live in the image, one per pixel at most: each sniffs the chemical trail ahead, left and right, turns toward the strongest scent, steps forward and lays more trail, so a transport network self-organises with a true hierarchy — thick pulsing trunks linking the food patches by near-shortest paths, medium veins, a fine dendritic mesh at the foraging front, and coarse and fine regions that drift across the dish. Food patches appear, feed and deplete, then reappear elsewhere, so trunks reroute and abandoned routes fade into ghost grooves etched in wet black slate. Seen from a tilted camera with depth of field: molten gold veins with thin-film shoulders and white-hot cores, cytoplasm shuttle-streaming along the trunks and reversing every ~40 s, a teal capillary web at their feet, glossy amber food droplets, raking key light with soft shadows and studio reflections. Bass heats the cores and swells the food, the music breathes the glow, beats spawn bursts of new agents at the food, mids brighten the capillaries and highs make the agents sparkle — the network itself is left to the mould.
title: Physarum

description: Lenia — microscopic glass animals that are alive. A real Lenia continuous cellular automaton runs every frame in the Orbium regime, where living tissue can only survive as discrete soliton creatures: each one seeded from the actual Orbium pattern, then holding its own shape purely through the kernel-and-growth law as it glides across the water. They swim at random headings, meet, fuse into twin-bodied hybrids, flare and burst apart; long-range crowding keeps collisions from flooding into a labyrinth, and new creatures keep hatching into empty water, so the population turns over forever. Four bioluminescent species (cyan, magenta, lime, amber) each carry their colour inside their own body. Rendered as translucent gel with real thickness: the deep-blue abyss refracts through each body, fresnel membranes and inner lamellae glow (iso-surfaces of the creature itself, so they move with it), a hot nucleus pulses, wet speculars catch a key light; behind them a deeper defocused layer of creatures drifts under faint god rays, with marine snow and bokeh in front. Bass lifts the bioluminescence, beats hatch extra creatures and send light pulses through the bodies, highs sparkle the snow.
title: Lenia

description: Ferrofluid — a dish of black magnetic liquid under three wandering magnets, raymarched in 3D. Above a critical field the mirror-smooth pool breaks into the Rosensweig instability: hedgehogs of sharp concave spikes grow in exact hexagonal shells over each magnet, the liquid mounds up beneath them, and where two magnets meet the spikes part along a seam. As the magnets drift, merge and separate, the spike fields rise, shrink, swirl and re-form, and the whole field slowly breathes so the dish keeps changing. Black-mirror shading with one inter-reflection bounce (spikes mirror their neighbours, the pool mirrors the hedgehogs), crisp studio softbox and coloured strip-light reflections sliding across the flanks as the camera orbits, an oily thin-film sheen at the spike bases, a gunmetal dish and an out-of-focus studio backdrop. Bass pumps the magnets so the spikes stand up with the low end, beats send a capillary ring across the pool, mids swirl the hedgehogs, levels brighten the strips, highs shiver the surface.
title: Ferrofluid

description: Oil Paint — a living oil painting laid down stroke by stroke. A structure-tensor flow field follows every contour of the scene, an anisotropic Kuwahara filter flattens it into clean areas of colour, and three coats of real brush strokes are splatted along the flow: big body strokes, a second coat and fine detail strokes on the edges, each one with its own pigment load (broken colour, a dirty-brush second tone, bristle streaks), a blunt loaded start that tapers dry, ragged bristle edges and a curve that bends with the flow. The paint has real thickness: ridges pushed to the stroke edges, bristle grooves and blobs where the brush landed are lit by a raking gallery light with wet sheen, groove occlusion and canvas weave in the thin passages. Three scenes cycle and repaint themselves as they move — a swirling starry nocturne with a flame cypress over wheat, a burning sunset over a field of sunflowers, and a gestural abstraction on a black ground — or bind any image and it is painted instead. Bass rakes the light lower so the impasto leaps out and pushes the swirl, beats catch the wet sheen, mids thicken the paint.
title: Oil Paint

description: Vortex Street — a real Lattice-Boltzmann fluid (D2Q9, nine particle distributions streaming and colliding on a grid, four solver steps every frame) flowing past bobbing cylinders and pitching plates in a dark water tunnel. Every body sheds a genuine Kármán vortex street: alternating whirlpools peel off, roll up and march downstream, and the wakes of staggered bodies collide, braid and break into turbulence. Each body bleeds its own ink — hot magenta, electric cyan, molten gold, acid lime — and where two wakes shear together the pigments blend into vermilion, indigo and green along the layers. Dye has real range: hair-fine wisps fade into black, translucent veils glow faintly, dense ink rises into glossy relief and the vortex eyes burn white-hot. A rake of fine streaklines enters from the left, bending around the bodies and curling into every vortex, over a dark tank floor with a faint caustic web and schlieren shimmer. Bass pushes the current harder, beats squeeze puffs of ink from every body, mids swing the plates, highs sparkle the gloss.
title: Vortex Street

description: Watercolor — a real wet-on-wet watercolor simulation that paints a whole painting on every sheet of cold-press paper. Water lives only on wet paper; the rim of each wash dries first and drifts the pigment outward into crisp tide lines, charges dropped into a wet wash feather and bleed along a divergence-free flow, clean water dropped into a drying wash grows cauliflower back-runs, and the finest pigment settles into the valleys of the paper tooth as granulation. The autonomous painter alternates Frankenthaler-scale gestural abstracts — three or four huge sweeping washes or poured pools per sheet, each in a harmonious triad (indanthrone · crimson · turquoise, orange · crimson · violet, turquoise · indanthrone · orange…), charged wet-in-wet, bloomed with clean water, finished with a few calligraphic dark accents and spatter, white paper breathing between them — with a loose atmospheric landscape: a graded sky with a lifted glow, sky blooms and soft clouds, mountain ranges dropped into the still-wet wash so they feather, and a warm ground. Pigments mix subtractively (Beer-Lambert) with a density cap so layered glazes stay luminous, the sheet cockles and its tooth catches a raking light, wet passages carry a moving gloss, and when a painting is finished a fresh sheet slides in over it with a drop shadow. Bass deepens the glaze, mids stir the flow, beats throw bigger spatter, highs sparkle the wet gloss.
title: Watercolor

description: Event Horizon — a Schwarzschild black hole rendered by integrating every light ray along its curved geodesic: light bends around the photon sphere, the back of the accretion disk is lifted into a halo over the top and under the bottom of the shadow, the starfield folds into an Einstein ring and a razor-thin photon ring hugs the darkness. The disk is a real volume of turbulent plasma in Keplerian rotation — inner rings whip round faster than the outer ones, stretching hot filaments into spiral streaks — coloured by a blackbody temperature profile, Doppler-beamed (the approaching side blazes blue-white, the receding side sinks to deep ember red) and gravitationally redshifted near the horizon. Faint relativistic jets lance out of the poles. Anamorphic bloom, ACES and the HD finish. Bass feeds the accretion rate, beats fire magnetic flares that orbit with the gas, mids churn the turbulence, highs sparkle hot clumps.
title: Event Horizon

description: Pixel Sort — a real sorting algorithm running live on the image. Inside every luminance interval the pixels are compared and swapped by an odd-even transposition sorting network — eight compare-swap steps every frame — so you watch the picture physically sort itself into molten streaks: chrome highlights slide down their columns, reflections stretch into rainbow drips, and whenever the source moves the sort starts over and chases it. A wandering re-sort wave keeps snapping columns back to the live image so the sorting never finishes; datamosh macroblocks drag old pixels along the motion and glitch slices tear the frame on beats. The internal source is an iridescent liquid-chrome sculpture over a black mirror floor lit by neon strip lights; bind any image or camera to Input and it sorts that instead. Bass feeds the datamosh and swells the sculpture, beats fire re-sort waves and RGB slice tears, the level opens the sort window, highs sparkle.
title: Pixel Sort

description: Erosion — a volcanic island at dusk carved live by a real hydraulic erosion simulation: rain falls from drifting storm cells, water flows through a virtual-pipe shallow-water solver, picks up sediment where it runs fast and steep and drops it where it slows, landslides slump the over-steep walls and slow isostatic rebound keeps the mountains rising so the land never wears flat. Rivers branch into a dendritic network that keeps reorganising: dark glossy threads that mirror the dusk sky, a hairline of cyan light burning in the thalweg of every big trunk (molten amber where it runs heavy with silt), white-water cascades down the cliffs and braided shallow sheets across the deltas; still water settles into dark mirror lakes; deltas build out into a black sea. Cutting reveals basalt strata with iron and ash seams. A low camera circles the island under a magenta afterglow with long sun shadows, storm shadows and sun glitter on the sea. Bass pours harder rain and surges the rivers, beats crack lightning inside the storms, highs sparkle the water.
title: Erosion

description: Ocean — a real spectral sea living through a slow weather arc. Dozens of Gerstner waves drawn from a wind-sea spectrum (long swells down to ripples, each at its true deep-water speed) plus capillary ripple octaves pile into sharp-crested water that a low camera rides between the swells, pitching and rolling with the sea. Every few minutes the light turns: a golden sunset with a crisp limb-darkened sun and a glitter path of thousands of micro-facet sparkles, then deep blue hour with an indigo sky, first stars and glowing teal crests, then a storm of bruised slate clouds, lightning and building whitecaps, then gold again. Thin crests glow with backlit subsurface light, the surface mirrors volumetric-looking clouds with lit undersides and silver linings, distance filters small waves into physically-based roughness so the horizon stays clean and the foreground razor sharp, and lacy foam with bubbles trails behind each breaking crest while spray lifts into the wind. Bass builds the sea state, beats flash lightning, level brightens glitter and foam, highs sparkle the ripples.
title: Ocean

description: Komorebi — sunlight falling through leaves into a quiet room, rendered from the real optics: every gap in the canopy is a pinhole camera, so each dancing spot of light on the plaster wall and oak floor is an image of the sun itself — round no matter what shape the gap is, larger the higher the leaf, stretched into ellipses where the low golden-hour beam rakes across the wall. A window frames the beam into panes, a sprig just outside throws soft leaf shadows, and the whole pattern swims and twinkles as wind gusts roll through the tree. Then a slow eclipse arrives: the moon bites into the sun and every one of the hundreds of spots turns into a crescent at once, narrows to a ring of fire at the annular peak, and swings back to round — the hidden physics of dappled light made visible. Dust drifts through window-shaped god rays that carry the same crescents, motes glint when they cross a beam, the plaster's trowel texture rises under the grazing light and the varnished floor holds a soft reflection of the wall. Bass gusts the wind through the canopy and lifts the sun, beats breathe the god rays, highs sparkle the motes.
title: Komorebi

description: Frost — real ice crystals growing on a window at sunrise. A Kobayashi phase-field solidification runs live (four solver steps every frame): the ice front grows where the glass is undercooled, its interface energy is sixfold anisotropic, latent heat released at the front slows its neighbours, and the instability splits every arm into dendrites with side branches, exactly how frost ferns and snowflake arms grow. Several crystals nucleate at different orientations, collide into grain boundaries and keep branching. The low winter sun shines through from behind: thin arms and growth tips burn gold-white, edges split into prismatic fringes, facets glint, and the clear glass around each crystal (vapour it has stolen) stays bright while the rest of the pane beads with condensation — every bead a tiny lens holding an upside-down sunrise. As the sun climbs the frost melts away from it in a warm front, the pane clears, and new crystals nucleate. Bass undercools the glass so the ice grows faster, beats nucleate new crystals, the level warms the sun, highs make the facets glint.
title: Frost

description: Fireflies — a meadow at the edge of a dark forest at dusk, filled with hundreds of fireflies that slowly learn to flash together. Every firefly is a coupled oscillator (the Kuramoto model): it keeps its own rhythm but nudges its phase toward the neighbours it can see, so the meadow drifts from scattered random twinkling into rolling waves of light that sweep across the grass and finally into whole-forest unison — like the synchronous fireflies of the Great Smoky Mountains — before the swarm scatters and starts learning again. Each flash is a real firefly pulse (a fast rise and a slower fade, with a little climb as it lights) in yellow-green with a few amber strays, scattering into the evening mist as physically integrated glow halos, lighting the grass tips, the blades around it and the nearest tree trunks. Layered forest silhouettes recede into blue haze under a deepening dusk sky with the first stars. Beats jolt the swarm and scatter its phases, bass swells the flashes, the level lifts the mist glow, highs twinkle the stars.
title: Fireflies

description: Prism — Newton's experimentum crucis staged as a light installation. A slit lamp throws a sheet of white light through a glass prism that fans it into a true spectrum; a second, inverted prism catches the fan and folds every colour back into a single white beam, which then strikes a slowly turning pentagonal crystal that shatters it again into several rainbows that stand as tall bars of colour on a dark matte screen. Every wavelength from deep violet to far red is traced on its own path through all three bodies — real Cauchy dispersion, Snell refraction, Fresnel losses and total internal reflection — and coloured through the CIE colour-matching functions, so overlapping spectra mix additively and fringes are real. Across the cycle the second prism drifts out of true (the white beam frays into colour), rises clear of the light entirely (the full fan swings across the screen as one huge rainbow), and drops back to snap the light white again, while the crystal's facets sweep its spectra up and down the screen. Dust hangs in every beam, the glass glows where the light runs through it, flares burn at each face, caustic glints spark on the floor beneath the glass, and the camera drifts between the whole installation and close macro views of the light leaving the glass. Bass brightens the lamp, beats shimmer the dust, mids nudge the crystal, highs sparkle the motes.
title: Prism

description: Rain Glass — a night-bus window in the rain, run by a real droplet simulation on the glass. Rain lands as drops of every size, neighbours coalesce, and once a drop is heavy enough it breaks loose and runs, meandering, swallowing the beads in its path and leaving a wet trail that the surface tension pulls apart into strings of tiny beads that slowly dry. Running water wipes clear tracks through the condensation, which fogs back over in its own time. Every drop is a tiny lens: inside it the city is tack-sharp and upside down, ringed by a dark rim with a bright caustic crescent and a glint, while beyond the glass the city melts into bokeh — neon signs, lit windows, sodium street lamps, headlights and tail lights streaking across wet asphalt. The bus pulls away from the lights and stops again, and while it drives the drops get dragged back across the pane. Rain swells from drizzle to downpour with lightning in the heaviest squalls. Bass and beats throw fresh rain at the glass, level brightens the city, mids pulse the neon, highs sparkle the glints.
title: Rain Glass

description: Dunes — a living desert grown by the Werner sand-slab model: every grain-packet on the field is a slab that the wind lifts, hops downwind and drops (more readily on sand than on bare clay, always in the wind-shadow behind a crest), and wherever a slope gets steeper than the angle of repose the sand avalanches, so real barchans and transverse dunes form, migrate, collide and calve by themselves. The field is raised into a raymarched desert at golden hour: razor slip faces falling into deep violet shadow, long sun shadows raking across the stoss slopes, wind ripples combed across every gentle face, grain-flow streaks on the avalanche faces, cracked clay flats between the dunes, quartz glints, sand blowing off the brinks as glowing plumes, giant draa swells under it all and heat shimmer on the horizon while a low camera glides across the sea of sand. Bass gusts the wind (more transport and saltation), beats send a wave of blowing sand across the field, the level warms the light, highs sparkle the quartz.
title: Dunes

description: Colored Shadows — an installation study in additive light, after Olafur Eliasson and Goethe's coloured shadows. Three coloured spotlights — red, green and blue — wash a tall white gallery wall, and where they overlap the light adds up to white. Every form in front of the wall blocks a different light from a different angle, so its shadows are never grey: block the red and the shadow glows cyan, block the green and it turns magenta, block the blue and it burns yellow, and where two shadows overlap only one pure primary is left — until all three meet in a core of true black. A slowly turning Calder-style mobile of hanging discs, a white ceramic sphere carved into a gyroid lattice on a plinth, and a pair of interlocked rings tumbling in the air throw crisp umbras ringed by soft rainbow penumbrae that slide, stretch and cross as the lights drift and take turns fading. A dark polished floor mirrors the wall, faint haze glows around each lamp and dust motes catch the beams. Bass swells the lamps, beats breathe the light, mids warm the haze, highs sparkle the dust.
title: Colored Shadows

description: Bioluminescent Shore — a night beach where the sea is alive with dinoflagellates. The plankton is a real excitable medium (a Barkley / FitzHugh–Nagumo model running two solver steps every frame on the water surface): mechanical shear excites it, it flashes electric blue, then goes refractory and has to recover before it can fire again. Breaking waves are the trigger — the curl of every breaker ignites and the light races along the lip and through the whitewater as a travelling excitation front, foam lace sparkles grain by grain, the swash glows as it runs up the sand and slides back, and an invisible walker leaves a trail of glowing footprints in the wet sand that fade behind them. Fish strike the surface and send rings of light across the calm water. Shoaling swell sets refract around the curved bay, crests steepen and break where the water gets too shallow, wet sand mirrors the glow, and above it all a dark headland with a sweeping lighthouse beam, the Milky Way and a sky full of pinpoint stars. Bass charges the plankton and lifts the sets, beats fire extra splashes and brighter flashes, mids feed the sparkle, highs twinkle the stars.
title: Bioluminescent Shore

description: Kelp — a giant-kelp forest where every strand is a real rope simulation: thirty-six stalks of linked nodes, each node buoyed upward by its gas bladders and dragged by a living current (a long ocean swell surging back and forth, a cross-swell, slow turbulence), integrated every frame and held to length node by node, so the forest leans, surges and recoils like the real thing. Long translucent golden blades with ruffled, rippling margins and a faint midrib stream off the stalks and glow as the sun comes through them, with little gas bladders at their bases. Sharp-edged sunbeams fan down through the gaps in the canopy, flickering with the surface waves and glittering with particles; overhead the surface shimmers with Snell's window and a rippling sun, caustics dance over up-facing blades and the sand, a milling bait ball of over a hundred silver fish circles and turns together, flashing as their flanks catch the light, and the camera glides slowly in, up and down through the forest while the water falls away to deep navy. Bass deepens the swell and the glow, beats push a surge through the forest and flash the caustics, mids stir the turbulence, highs sparkle the fish and the drifting particles.
title: Kelp

description: Light Painting — long-exposure photography as physics. Glowing LED wands swing on damped-pendulum harmonograph paths through 3D space while the camera's shutter stays open: every frame the light is integrated into a persistent sheet of film, so the wands paint thick luminous ribbons — gel gradients across their width, fine LED-pixel streaks along their length, a white-hot core where the hand holds the light — that fold over themselves and flare brightest wherever a ribbon turns edge-on to the lens. The pendulums lose energy, so each plate spirals inward into a tighter figure before the next plate begins with new ratios and new gels while the old exposure slowly fades. Steel-wool sparks burst from the wand, fly ballistically under drag and gravity and cool from white through amber to red. The film itself responds like film: a Hurter–Driffield curve rolls the highlights into white, red halation glows around the hottest strokes, grain lives in the mid-tones. Bass pushes more light into the exposure, beats throw spark bursts and flare the cores, mids widen the ribbons, highs sparkle the LEDs.
title: Light Painting

description: Cells — a gallery of living specimens under a fluorescence microscope. Each tile is a raymarched block of tissue whose surface is grown from an animated 3D Voronoi foam: honeycomb pits, drooping scales, ring cells, plated domes, pebble clusters, budding blobs, fibrous mats, smooth caverns and a thermal-imaged well. Twelve species, each slowly morphing into the next on its own clock, so the grid never repeats in lockstep. Lighting is emissive and false-coloured like confocal imaging — deep navy cavities, royal blue and cyan walls, acid-green rims, red-orange glow pooled in the pits — and the whole image is resolved as a fine point-cloud stipple. Bass swells the cells, beats send a fluorescent wave through every specimen, mids drift the hue, highs make the stipple sparkle.
title: Cells

description: Marble — a cabinet of living glass orbs. Every sphere holds its own slowly churning 3D flow field (iterated domain warp sampled on the rotating sphere), read out through interference and thermal colour maps: black voids, deep blue, cyan, acid yellow, ember orange and red fringes. Six families of orb share the grid — vivid fringe orbs, soft defocused glass, kaleidoscopic mandalas, ghost orbs whose shell disappears so only the coloured blob floats, ochre marbled agate with contour lines, and dark void orbs threaded with cyan filaments — and each orb drifts from one family into the next on its own clock. A travelling light sweeps the grid, every orb bobs and breathes, beats ripple a light ring outward from the centre, bass churns the flow, mids slide the colour bands, highs light up the rims.
title: Marble

description: Shrooms — rows of soft, gradient-dyed mushroom stalks dancing in 3D. Each stalk is a bent, bulbous capsule smooth-blended into a rounded cap, swaying on its own spring with a phase lag along the row so waves of motion roll through the crowd; bass squashes and stretches them like a bounce, beats kick a wiggle that ripples down the line, mids widen the sway, highs shimmer the grain. Colour is a living gradient up each stalk (pale foot → glowing body → dark cap) that slowly flows and drifts. The scene morphs continuously between three looks: Aurora (a tall merged wall of drips in maroon, blue, cream, lavender and red), Ember Rows (three stacked tiers of slim dark-capped stalks fading red → pink → butter) and Cobalt Cluster (a few fat blue clubs fading to white on warm paper).
title: Shrooms

description: Objectos — a wobbly totem of 3 to 6 soft 3D objects (spheres, fat rings, clover crosses, puffy flowers, twin blobs, rounded cubes, pills, pucks) balanced on top of each other and dancing. A real spring–damper simulation runs every frame in a tiny persistent buffer: each object has its own squash-and-stretch spring and two lean springs coupled to the one beneath it, so motion travels up the stack with lag and overshoot like jelly; the whole totem hops on beats, lands, and squashes on impact. Bass compresses the stack, beats make it jump, mids add a rubbery wobble and twist, highs make the glossy highlights flare. Each slot slowly morphs into another shape, and the materials keep trading — glossy black, glowing gradient, dark-rimmed matte, stripes, dots, checks, iridescent — in a palette pulled from the references (signal red, cyan, maroon, pink, lavender, ink).
title: Objectos

description: Hourglass — a living hourglass that keeps pinching thin and swelling thick. Its silhouette is a mirrored profile of two lobes meeting at a neck; the lobes breathe, change shape (round, teardrop, diamond, lamp-shade), wiggle and drift, while three looks flow into each other: Nested Rings (an infinite tunnel of tangent circles stacked into the neck, each a radial rainbow), Thin Film (glowing interference fringes around dark lobes holding a sun and a target), and Lathe (a turned 3D vessel whose rainbow sweeps around it as it spins). Over it all runs a film and glitch layer: travelling pixelation zones, block mosaics, RGB split, slice tears, gate weave, flicker and grain. Bass pinches and swells the neck, beats fire glitch bursts and pixel drops, mids feed the wiggle, highs push the chroma split.
title: Hourglass

description: Zebra — stripes drawn on a liquid sheet. A heightfield made of flowing domain-warped waves, drifting bumps and beat-launched ripples is raymarched from a tilting camera, so the lines bend over real 3D folds, hide behind ridges, catch speculars and throw self-shadows. Six looks morph into each other: Satin (glossy black-and-white fabric), Op-Art (Riley-style gradient bands, orange to violet to cobalt to lime), Neon Spectrum (each line a full rainbow ribbon on black), Glitch Chroma (monochrome lines that split into RGB wherever the liquid is steep), Holo Chrome (thin silver lines over iridescent oil-slick colour) and Glow Lines (emissive line drawing floating on black). Stripes flow along the sheet, the camera breathes, and the RGB split follows the slope. Bass lifts the waves, beats fire ripples and a chroma kick, mids stir the flow, highs make the speculars and split flare.
title: Zebra
